### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **58** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**98** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2`.

⛔ **16** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/identity/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **2** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`, `packageId (4 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `PERMISSION_DENIED (literal, 51 pages)`, `sys_user (literal, 48 pages)`
- **16** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `061d34e2bd151348b0277ed934f6b5968fa3ad3c` — the merge of head `deedb538e508cb01955a0a03192fa39a457a3ddb` into base `81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 061d34e2bd151348b0277ed934f6b5968fa3ad3c && git checkout 061d34e2bd151348b0277ed934f6b5968fa3ad3c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2 deedb538e508cb01955a0a03192fa39a457a3ddb && git checkout -B drift-repro 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2 && git merge --no-ff deedb538e508cb01955a0a03192fa39a457a3ddb

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 81cd9eb0e9f2fb32a9ae01ef60dc4da45f892ef2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `805f0481cdb41bd386ae7bb4b4710b9ff47f7cc2`
Local-runs: none

Read: card #29443 (body and all 5 comments, including seat ruling 6583289013 and dev report 6586486609), parent ruling 6570568131 on #28971, the PR body, its 32-file list, the net diff, and the check-runs on this head. The cited code was read on `origin/main`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies**

| Change | Judgment |
|:--|:--|
| New platform object `sys_personal_view`, served at `/api/v1/data/sys_personal_view` (read, create, edit) | **Right.** It is on the `sys_user_preference` template that ruling C names. It is `private`, `system-data`, and declares the owner-only `defaultRowScope` with `operation: 'all'`. The organization column puts it behind the Layer 0 wall. The id is a nanoid, so it never takes the `object.key` form (pinned). |
| `member_default` grants r/c/e on the object and no delete | **Right.** ADR-0090 D5 keeps delete off the anchor. The generic `DELETE` stays 403, pinned at both the engine and REST levels. |
| `organization_admin` names the object without `viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords` | **Right.** This is the `sys_audit_log` per-object pattern. `resolveObjectPermission` (`permission-evaluator.ts`) prefers the explicit entry, so the bypass is closed for both variants. Ablation 1 is red as described. |
| Save-time `ListViewSchema` check: `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` with paths under `config` | **Right.** It uses an existing code, refuses on create and on update-with-config, and leaves stored bodies unchanged (pinned). |
| `is_default` column, plus a hook that keeps one default per owner and object | **Wrong: M1.** The card's In-list says "set as my default (**reuse the existing pin**)". The existing pin is the Console's per-object `LIST_PINNED_VIEW_PREFERENCE` (#27594, `ObjectView.tsx`), which already stores a view id. This PR adds a second, server-side default store beside it. Neither the PR body nor the dev report flags this as a deviation. |
| New route `DELETE /api/v1/personal-views/:id` | **Right in mechanism**; see "Security of the door" below. The ledger row (`gap`), the route-envelope declaration and the single-authz-resolver delegator row are all present. The closed query set is empty and refused with 400 (AGENTS.md route rule 5). When no `DELETE` verb exists, the door is skipped with a warning that names it (rule 3). |
| `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_personal_view` | **Right.** The registry's maintenance contract requires it, and #27123 and #27185 set the precedent. One side effect: `stack.zod.ts` now accepts a top-level action whose `objectName` is `sys_personal_view` (`isPlatformProvidedObjectName`). This is a widening, and #27123 classed it as "not an authorable surface". |
| CLI organization-ownership inventory row, i18n extract and 4 bundles, tenancy census (92 / 47), tenant-audit census (256) with its hand-written figures | **Right.** Each one is derived, and the gates that own them are listed under check-runs below. |

**Security of the door**
- **Refusal order is correct.** The pre-read refusals (401, the held sign-in's 403, the query 400, 503) do not depend on the row. The row is then read as the caller, so an unknown id and an unreadable row get the same 404. A member or an organization administrator cannot use the door to learn that a row exists.
- **The 403 leaks nothing.** It reaches only a caller who can already read the row (a platform administrator).
- **Attribution is right.** `attributedUserId` is the caller and `tenantId` is the caller's organization, both pinned in `personal-view-routes.test.ts`.
- **Other read paths are closed.**
  - Generic data API: row scope applies (pinned).
  - Export: the engine reads as the caller, and nothing grants `allowExport` on the object.
  - Search: `searchable: false`.
  - `/meta/view`: pinned 404.
  - `expand`: no lookup points at the object.
  - Realtime: no external transport is mounted on main.
  - Audit ledger: rows about the record are parent-record-gated (`audit-log-read-visibility.ts`), so an organization administrator without the ledger audit capability sees none of them, and delete rows are excluded.
- **The platform administrator is not limited to reading. This is M2.** `ADMIN_FULL_ACCESS_CAPABILITIES` (`spec/src/identity/eval-user.zod.ts`) carries `allowDelete`, `allowEdit` and `modifyAllRecords` on `'*'`. The `owner_only_*` policies bind `org_member` only. So by the cited code, `admin_full_access` also PATCHes and DELETEs a member's view through `/api/v1/data/sys_personal_view/:id`. (This was read from source, not driven.) No test pins that path.
  - That makes three statements false: the PR body's 「但他删不了（答 403）」 ("but he can't delete it, answers 403"), the risk line, and the open question's premise "The delete door already refuses its delete with 403".
  - The door's 403 is still correct for the door itself. It just does not stop the platform administrator.

**The four forced test edits are legitimate. None loosens a guard.**
- `default-row-scope-declarations.test.ts`: the ruling's 23 `DECLARERS` and their length pin are unchanged. The new `DECLARED_AT_BIRTH` set adds a stronger assertion: the literal is exact and no shipped set carries a copy.
- `bundle-ownership.test.ts`: this is the guard's own instruction for a new extract-config object.
- `route-ledger-live-mount-parity.dogfood.test.ts`: it adds a ledger to the union and exempts nothing. The input is declared in `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs` and `turbo.json`.
- `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts`: the SCIM stamp really does register under `packageId: 'com.objectstack.plugin-auth'` (`auth-plugin.ts` on main), and the assertions are unchanged.

**Check-runs on this head**

There are 65 runs: 58 success, 7 skipped, and none failed or pending.
- The success runs include every Test Core shard (1/8–8/8), the four Type Check families, every Lint family including PM dispatch-gates, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset, Spec property liveness and Governed Surface Queue Guard.
- The 7 skipped runs are opt-in or matrix-gated: UI Published Artifacts, Temporal Conformance, the Schedule gate, Packed-tarball smoke, Dogfood Verify CLI, the Dogfood shard matrix and the 18.x upgrade harness.
- The gates are green. Neither must-fix below is something a gate measures.

**Must-fix**
- **M1: the `is_default` default store is an undisclosed deviation from the card.** The card says "reuse the existing pin". There are two ways to fix it:
  - drop `is_default` and the `keepOneDefault` hooks, so the ui lane pins a personal view's id through `LIST_PINNED_VIEW_PREFERENCE`; or
  - get a seat ruling recorded on #29443 that replaces the pin, and flag the deviation in the PR body and the dev report.

  As the PR stands, the ui lane gets two "my default" stores and no rule for which one wins.
- **M2: the PR states the platform-administrator boundary wrongly.**
  - Pin what is really there: as `admin_full_access`, the generic `GET`, `PATCH` and `DELETE` on a member's view, beside the existing door-403 pin.
  - Correct the 维护者速读 (maintainer quick-read) risk line, the What-changes bullet, the changeset bullet (which says "still reads" and omits edit and delete) and the open question's premise.

**Should-fix**
- **S1: a code comment overstates what the `private` posture does.** `sys-personal-view.object.ts` says "An application's wildcard set never widens who reads another reader's views". That holds only for a non-superuser wildcard. ADR-0066 D2 lets a `'*'` entry that carries `viewAllRecords` or `modifyAllRecords` reach a `private` object. Say "a plain (non-superuser) wildcard".
- **S2: external members get no grant.** `external_default` (`EXTERNAL_DEFAULT_PERMISSION_SET`) replaces `member_default` for `org_external` and carries `sys_user_preference` but not `sys_personal_view`. An external reader therefore cannot save a view, while the card's ui step says "save-as-my-view available to any reader". Either add the same r/c/e line there, or record externals as out of scope so the ui lane hides the button for them.
- **S3: the door duplicates the unreact door.** `personal-view-routes.ts` is a near line-for-line second copy of `comment-reaction-routes.ts` (caller resolver, handler and the removal core). File a follow-up to extract one shared own-row removal door before a third copy appears. This does not block the PR.

**Nits**
- If M1 keeps the default rule, `keepOneDefault` does not hold under concurrent writes or a predicate update, which carries no id. That contradicts the hook's "two tabs cannot leave two defaults".
- `config.data.object` is not checked against `object_name`.
- An owner re-parenting `user_id` on update is held by the row scope's post-image check, but nothing pins it.

### ② Semver level

- **`patch` on all five packages is right.** AGENTS.md (Post-Task Checklist step 3) says "the level follows the kind alone … `none` takes `patch`". The `feat(...)` prefix does not set the level.
  - `Metadata-protocol: none` holds. A platform object holding user data is not an author key, value or metadata type, and `/meta` does not serve it (pinned).
  - #27185 is the direct precedent: `feat(platform-objects)`, a new system object, and patch for platform-objects, spec and cli, with `Metadata-protocol: none`.
- **`@objectstack/spec` belongs in the changeset.** It publishes the changed `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE` constant. A publishing change takes a changeset, never none, and #27123 and #27185 both list spec as patch for exactly this row.
- **Clause-②: yes (widening) is right.** It adds a served object and a served route, and no existing answer narrows: the generic delete is still 403 (pinned). Both declaration lines appear in the PR body and in the changeset. Check Changeset is green.
- **M2 also reaches the changeset text.** Its "A platform administrator's bare `admin_full_access` wildcard still reads every row" understates edit and delete, and that text ships as `CHANGELOG.md`.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev's open question: should `admin_full_access` keep reading members' views?**
Answer: **A** for this card, kept as a recorded boundary and decided together with `sys_user_preference`. Platform administrators are the deployment's operators, and the rescue path depends on the bare wildcard. But the premise has to be corrected first (M2): today the boundary is read, edit and delete through the data door, not read only. If the maintainer is asked, the question must say so.

**Dev flags (deviations)**
1. Spec in the changeset: **kept**; see ②. The card forbids a spec *schema key*. This is a registry row, not a key.
2. The four forced test edits: **legitimate**; see ①.
3. Route name `/api/v1/personal-views/:id`: **recommend accept.**
   - It is plural and kebab-case per AGENTS.md naming ("REST endpoints → plural"; compare `/api/v1/share-links`).
   - It takes the record id in the path, with an empty, refused query set, like the unreact door.
   - It cannot sit under `/api/v1/data/…` (route rule 1, one route, one owner).
   - This is the seat's call.
4. Base Clause-② read from source: **accepted.** On base, no registrar names the route, and the object is not registered.
5. The `/meta` pin is structural, and the no-bypass pin does not react to ablation 1: **accepted as explained.**
6. Dist ablations rebuilt with `OS_SKIP_DTS=1`: **noted.** CI on this head is the gate.
7. Earlier base-red batteries fixed by #29451: **not re-judged.** The final battery ran on this head.
8. Fork 2 moved from B to A mid-card: **matches** seat ruling 6583289013. The PR says `Fixes #29443` for the server step.

**Escalated**
- **The review tier is in doubt.** `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` reads the `schema` face (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER) off `packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts`. This record is the TIER_DEFAULT declaration review the brief ordered. The seat should confirm whether the next head also owes a CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER record.
- **The claim names no spec exception.** The claim (6580568459) says "⛔ No `packages/spec/**`", and the PR cites a seat ruling allowing the one-line spec touch. No such ruling is on the card. The card body forbids only a spec schema key, which this is not. The seat should record the allowance on the card.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `deedb538e508cb01955a0a03192fa39a457a3ddb`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.test.ts, packages/spec/src/stack.zod.ts, packages/lint/src/validate-object-references.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-personal-view.object.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/manifest.ts

Round 2 of the review on #29575, per seat ruling 6587007982 point 8: the spec roster path at this tier, and the rest of the 32-file diff judged in this same record as the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` (declaration face). Read: card #29443 (body and all 8 comments, including round-1 record 6586971553, the seat's round-2 ruling 6587007982 and dev report 6589962356), the PR body, the file list, the net diff against `main`, and the check-runs on this head. The cited code was read on `origin/main` at `5bd615ef`. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

### ① Derived judgments

**Round-1 findings and ruling points on this head**

| Item | Status on `deedb538` |
|:--|:--|
| Ruling 1, spec allowance | **Met.** The only `packages/spec/**` path in the file list is the roster line; one line, alphabetically placed (`sys_organization` to `sys_platform_setting`). `@objectstack/spec: patch` is in the changeset. |
| M1 / ruling 2, one default store | **Met.** No `is_default` column and no one-default hook remain in the diff. The object's docblock, the hooks' docblock and the changeset all say the default is the Console's pin. The dev's claim about the pin is **true on `main`**: `LIST_PINNED_VIEW_PREFERENCE` (`ui/packages/app-shell/src/utils/workspacePreference.ts`) stores `{"view": VIEW_ID, "v": 1}` and `fromRecord` accepts any non-empty string; `ObjectView.tsx` resolves it with `resolveViewId(pinnedViewChoice, views.map(v => v.id), objectDef.name)`, whose first step (`ui/packages/core/src/utils/resolve-view-id.ts`) is an exact-id match, and the two qualification steps only ever add or strip the `OBJECT.` prefix, so a nanoid with no `.` is matched as itself or not at all. It works once the ui half lists personal views in `views`; no second store. |
| M2 / ruling 3, platform administrator | **Met.** `admin_full_access` is untouched. The generic GET, PATCH and DELETE of a member's view are pinned at the engine (`personal-view-hooks.test.ts`, two RECORDED BOUNDARY tests) and over REST (`[platform-admin] RECORDED BOUNDARY`). The PR body, the changeset bullet and open question 1 now say read, edit and delete; the false 403 sentence is gone. Only the door refuses the platform admin, as the body says. |
| S1 / ruling 4, object comment | **Met.** `sys-personal-view.object.ts` now says a plain (non-superuser) wildcard does not reach a `private` object and one carrying `viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords` still does (ADR-0066 D2), naming both sets. |
| S2 / ruling 5, external members | **Met.** `external_default` is untouched (no `sys_personal_view` line in the diff). The PR body and the changeset say externals get no grant in this version; it is open question 2 for the ui half. |
| Ruling 6, route name | Accepted by the seat; `DELETE /api/v1/personal-views/:id` unchanged. |
| Ruling 7 nits | **Met.** The `user_id` re-parent refusal is pinned (engine, member and platform admin; REST, owner) with an echo control. The `config.data.object` vs `object_name` check is a refusal, `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `config.data.object` (code `object_mismatch`), on create and on update (three pins plus a control at engine level, one over REST). |
| S3 | Follow-up, the seat's card. Not in this PR, as ruled. |
| Round-1 forced edit to `durability-swallow-repair.test.ts` | Reverted; three forced test edits remain and were judged legitimate in round 1. |

**Accept-set and public-surface changes the diff implies**

| Change | Judgment |
|:--|:--|
| `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `sys_personal_view` | **Right.** The roster's maintenance contract (module header on `main`) requires the line, and `platform-object-names.test.ts` holds each group equal to the objects its package's `*.object.ts` files declare, so the line and the new object file are one change. Derived accept-set widenings on `main`: `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` now admits the name at rung ③ of `validate-object-references.ts`, in `validate-nav-access.ts` and `validate-translation-references.ts`, and `stack.zod.ts` accepts a top-level action whose `objectName` is `sys_personal_view`. Each is a reference to a real registered object, the #27123 / #27185 class; none is an author-writable key. `dangling-reference-audit.ts` reads only the `plugin-security` group, so it is unchanged. |
| New platform object served at `/api/v1/data/sys_personal_view` (read, create, edit) | **Right.** On the `sys_user_preference` template: `private`, `system-data`, owner-only `defaultRowScope` with `operation: 'all'`, organization column, `nameField: 'label'`. |
| **The new save rule: a non-system update that changes `user_id` is refused `403 PERMISSION_DENIED`, platform administrators included** | **Right, and the diagnosis is correct on `main`.** `collectRLSPolicies` (`security-plugin-object-inputs.ts`, header in `security-plugin.ts` and `object-default-row-scope.ts`) applies an object's `defaultRowScope` only when the held collection for that object AND operation is empty, and a held `'*'` policy counts. `member_default` carries `owner_only_writes` (`object: '*'`, `operation: 'update'`, `created_by == current_user.id`, `positions: ['org_member']`). So for a member's UPDATE on `sys_personal_view` the collection is that floor alone, and the object's `user_id == current_user.id` scope never enters the update gate: pre-image and post-image (`rls-compiler.ts`, `check` defaults to `using`) both pass on a row the member created, whatever `user_id` becomes. Reads and creates still collect the default (no held `'*'` policy for `select` or `insert`), which is why the row stays unreadable to others and a planted create is refused. A save rule is the right instrument: the floor is `member_default`'s and platform-wide. |
| Can any path still re-parent a view? | **No non-system path found.** The hook reads `ctx.previous`, and on `main` every `beforeUpdate` dispatch binds it: the by-id path reads the prior row before the dispatch and refuses an absent row with 404 (`engine.ts`, the #7867 gate); the predicate path dispatches per matched row with that row as `previous` (`engine-hook-dispatch.ts#dispatchPerRowBeforeHooks`); the whole-operation dispatch (`dispatchUnscopedMultiWriteHooks`) reaches only hooks flagged `dispatchUnscopedMultiWrite`, which this one is not, and the per-row dispatch still follows it. The REST import and the generic batch (`packages/rest/src/data-action-routes.ts`, `runImport`) write under the caller's own context (`isSystem` is set only on the `sys_import_job` rows), so an upsert's update is judged as the caller. A create naming another owner is refused by the row scope (pinned). |
| The `isSystem` skip | **Sound as a platform-writer skip, incomplete as stated.** `buildSession` carries `isSystem` only from the execution context (`engine-execution-plumbing.ts`). No shipped system writer updates `sys_personal_view`; the door deletes. But app-authored automation elevated to system does carry `isSystem`: a `runAs: 'system'` flow, a hook's `runAs: 'system'` / `sudo()`, an action body (`flow-system-identity-write-refusal.ts` describes the family, and refuses it for four identity objects only). Such a flow can re-parent a view. It is admin-authored metadata, and the platform admin's reach is the ruled posture, so this is not a hole in the rule; it is a sentence missing from census row 26c and the hooks' docblock. **S1 below.** |
